questions.q: Why does `Test-OverlookHealth` check more than just whether the database is reachable?
options: Because dbatools requires at least three checks per script
Because a check that only confirms the database is up misses most of what Chapters 2-4 actually built — TDE and backup recency need to be re-verified too
Because uptime checks are technically impossible in PowerShell
Because Azure SQL has no concept of 'online' status
questions.explain: Real health for this database means the security and recovery posture built earlier in this capstone is still actually true, not just that the server responds.

questions.q: Why does the script re-check TDE encryption_state specifically?
options: TDE cannot be checked more than once
Because Chapter 3's security posture is only real if it's still true later — a health check that never re-verifies TDE would miss real configuration drift
Because TDE needs to be re-enabled manually every day
Because encryption_state changes automatically every hour
questions.explain: Configuration can drift after initial setup; re-verifying it is exactly what a real health check is for.

questions.q: What does the `RecentBackup` check connect back to from earlier in this path?
options: Chapter 2's Bicep deployment
The Beginner capstone's backup discipline and Lesson 11's RPO target — a backup older than 24 hours is a problem worth surfacing before it becomes a disaster-recovery problem
Chapter 6's Data Factory pipeline
Nothing; it's unrelated to any other chapter
questions.explain: Catching a stale backup early prevents it from silently becoming a real DR gap later.

questions.q: Why does the script wrap all three checks into one function returning an OverallHealthy flag, rather than three separate scripts?
options: PowerShell requires all checks to be in one function
So Lesson 19's alerting logic can ask one simple question — is OverallHealthy false — instead of needing to know about TDE, backups, and database state individually
To make the script run slower on purpose
There is no real benefit; it's just a style preference
questions.explain: Pushing complexity into one well-defined function keeps everything built on top of it — like alerting — simple.

questions.q: What does `$health.Values -contains $false` actually determine in this script?
options: Whether any individual check failed, which flips OverallHealthy to false if so
The total number of checks run
Whether the database is online specifically
Whether the script itself encountered a runtime error
questions.explain: If any of the individual boolean checks is false, OverallHealthy becomes false — a single summary flag built from all three checks.
